record.paper_title: A Nonequilibrium Statistical Ensemble Formalism. Maxent-Nesom: Concepts, Construction, Application, Open Questions and Criticisms
record.original_question: How can nonequilibrium statistical mechanics reconcile reversible microscopic mechanical laws with irreversible macroscopic behavior, including Eddington's time-arrow, when the differential equations of mechanics themselves do not contain an analogue of the second law of thermodynamics and a statistical description must depend on assumptions about initial conditions, macroscopic coarse graining, and damping of correlations?

evidence.quote: How can we reconcile the reversibility of microscopic mechanics with the irreversibility of macroscopic behavior?
Another point of contention is the long standing question about macroscopic irreversibility in nature.

Since in the differential equations of mechanics themselves there is absolutely nothing analogous to the second law of thermodynamics, the latter can be mechanically represented only by means of assumptions regarding initial conditions.

artifact.status_search_result: The reconciliation of microscopic reversibility with macroscopic irreversibility is a classical foundational question (Loschmidt, Zermelo, Boltzmann, Eddington) that remains a subject of active debate and research. While many partial answers exist (Boltzmann's H-theorem with molecular chaos, BBGKY truncations, Lanford's theorem for hard spheres in the Boltzmann–Grad limit, projection-operator methods, decoherence-based arguments, MaxEnt/NESOM approaches, typicality arguments by Lebowitz, Goldstein and others), there is no universally accepted rigorous derivation of the second law from reversible microscopic dynamics under minimal assumptions. The problem is widely regarded as open in its general form.

status_evidence.title: Boltzmann's Approach to Statistical Mechanics
status_evidence.snippet: Lebowitz and others have argued for typicality-based explanations of the arrow of time, but a fully general rigorous derivation remains lacking.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational question still debated; partial answers via typicality.

status_evidence.title: Lanford's theorem and the Boltzmann equation
status_evidence.snippet: Lanford proved validity of the Boltzmann equation for hard spheres only for short times in the Boltzmann–Grad limit.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous derivations of irreversible macroscopic equations exist only in limited regimes.
